successors.name: Chenla
successors.text: all of Funan: the Mekong delta, the Cambodian south and the Gulf coast, 'annexed Funan' (Book of Sui, 636), 'in the beginning of the Zhenguan era (627–649)' (New Book of Tang)

ledger.x: 50: Funan established in the Mekong delta.

c. 220: Fan Shiman's conquests make the isthmus polities Funan's tributaries. 'Funan reached the apex of its power under the 3rd-century king Fan Shiman', who 'attacked more than ten kingdoms'; 'Funanese kings of the 2nd century conquered polities on the isthmus itself'.…

c. 598: Bhavavarman I and Citrasena attack Funan. 'Chenla was recognized by a foreign power as a separate political entity at the end of the sixth century'; Bhavavarman I 'built a temple in 598'; the two 'attacked Funan together and subdued it around 627–649'. The start year is bridged from the temple date; blend…
627: the isthmus tributaries released at Funan's end.
627: the fighting ends in Chenla's favour.

wars.name: Funan and Linyi attack Tongking (270s)
wars.outcome: 'In the 270s, Funan and Linyi jointly attacked Tongking', 'a brief conflict'; no border moved.

wars.name: Chenla's conquest of Funan (c. 598–627)
wars.outcome: Bhavavarman I and Citrasena Mahendravarman 'attacked Funan together and subdued it around 627–649'; Chenla 'annexed Funan' (Book of Sui, 636).

certainty.note: A mandala with no recorded frontier; the shape is Cliopatria's throughout, and the isthmus tributaries are a tint whose extent is the researcher's.
